reports.title: Technical Annex on the Adult Social Care Relative Needs Formula (ASC RNF)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG)
reports.description: Technical annex to the Fair Funding Review 2.0 consultation, feeding the Local Government Finance Settlement's Adult Social Care funding formula. Its §5 'Data and technical definitions' is a per-indicator data-source table naming exact statistical releases and table codes — this branch's UK analog to the Dutch Toelichting and Ontario's OMPF Appendix F. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: PDF downloaded and text-extracted in full (pypdf).
reports.cadence_note: Published as part of the Fair Funding Review 2.0 consultation cycle rather than a fixed annual schedule; filed as annual as the nearest available cadence.

release_schedule.note: This technical annex was published 20 June 2025 as a supporting document to the Fair Funding Review 2.0 consultation, which ran 20 June 2025 to 15 August 2025 and is now closed. The government stated it would set out its response and final policy positions in a Policy Statement in autumn 2025, ahead of the provisional Local Government Finance Settlement. The finalized ASC RNF was subsequently incorporated into MHCLG's 'Additional national available funding for adult social care' guidance (published 10 Feb 2026, updated 12 May 2026) as part of the 2026-27 to 2028-29 settlement. No fixed review cycle or recurring publication schedule for this specific technical annex was found; the Fair Funding Review 2.0 document itself only speaks generally of wanting funding data 'updated at planned intervals' without specifying a periodicity. This corroborates the existing cadence_note that the document is tied to the (irregular, non-fixed) Fair Funding Review consultation cycle rather than any fixed annual schedule.

reports.title: Local authority revenue expenditure and financing, England
reports.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG)
reports.description: MHCLG's compiled national statistical release of English local-authority revenue expenditure and financing — the direct structural parallel to Alberta's `ab-municipalaffairs-financial-statistical-data` and the Netherlands' `nl-cbs-iv3-gemeenten`. Accredited Official Statistics under the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: technical-notes page fetched and parsed in full.
reports.cadence_note: Published in stages through the year — a first release (early-September data cut-off) and a second/final release (mid-November cut-off) per financial year, per the technical notes' own 'Response rate and grossing' section.

entries.covers: Local authority revenue expenditure and financing, England: 2025 to 2026 - first release (Sept 2025 data cut-off)
Local authority revenue expenditure and financing, England: 2025 to 2026 - second/final release (Nov 2025 data cut-off)

release_schedule.note: MHCLG's own technical notes state: "The current schedule for publication of Local Authority Revenue Expenditure and Financing is a 'first release' in early Autumn, and a second release in December" (with further updates as data allow), matching the corpus's existing cadence_note of 2 releases/year (Sept data cut-off, Nov data cut-off). The first release for the 2025-26 financial year is confirmed on GOV.UK's upcoming-statistics calendar for 17 September 2026. The corresponding second/final release for 2025-26 has not yet been given a confirmed date on the calendar; the December entry below is an implied projection from the stated schedule, not a confirmed date.

reports.title: Revenue Outturn (RO) forms
reports.description: The standardised financial return every English local authority must complete annually, covering general fund revenue account transactions — the direct English counterpart to Alberta's Financial Information Return (FIR) and the Netherlands' Iv3-rapportage.
reports.cadence_note: Submitted in two stages per financial year: provisional figures (deadline late July) then certified figures (deadline mid-October), per MHCLG's technical notes.

release_schedule.note: MHCLG's annual letter to local authorities states: 'The RO 2025-26 return is due by Friday 24 July 2026' (provisional outturn, already passed as of today, 2026-08-11) and 'a certified return is emailed by Friday 9 October 2026'. This is an annual cycle: forms are distributed to English local authorities in April, provisional figures due late July, and a certified/final return due mid-October, each covering the financial year that ended the preceding March. Prior-year technical notes confirm the same pattern (2024-25 cycle: 'deadline for provisional RO figures was set for late July in 2025' and 'certified RO figures was set for mid-October'). The exact day (a specific Friday) shifts slightly year to year, so no single fixed rule sentence (e.g. 'by the fourth Friday of July') was found stated verbatim by the publisher; only year-specific letters give the exact dates. releases_per_year=1 on file is a reasonable simplification of what is really a two-stage (provisional + certified) annual return cycle for each financial year's data.

reports.title: Estimates of the population for England and Wales

entries.covers: Mid-2026 population estimates for England and Wales

release_schedule.note: ONS's own methodology page (Mid-year population estimates QMI) states estimates are 'normally published annually in June', but actual releases have deviated from that stated rule in recent years: mid-2023 estimates were released 8 October 2024, mid-2024 estimates were released 30 July 2025, and mid-2025 estimates were released 29 July 2026 (roughly 13 months after each mid-year reference point). Given the two most recent editions both landed in late July, the projected next edition (mid-2026 estimates) is estimated for around July 2027, but each bulletin itself lists 'Next release: To be announced' rather than a committed date, so this is an inference from the observed pattern, not a published calendar or firm rule.

reports.title: Code of Practice on Local Authority Accounting in the United Kingdom (the Code)
reports.description: The accounting standard every English local authority's Statement of Accounts must follow — the UK functional equivalent of `psab-psas` and the Netherlands' `nl-bbv`. Legal basis, VERIFIED DIRECTLY (legislation.gov.uk): Local Government Act 2003 s.21(2) creates the 'proper practices' concept and delegates identifying the actual standard to regulations; The Local Authorities (Capital Finance and Accounting) (England) Regulations 2003, reg. 31 names the CIPFA Code specifically as that standard. Note: this is a two-instrument statutory chain, not one — the Accounts and Audit Regulations 2015 uses the phrase 'proper practices' but does not itself name CIPFA in the provisions checked this session.
reports.cadence_note: Issued in dated annual editions (e.g. '2024/25', '2026/27'), unlike the Netherlands' BBV which amends continuously without dated editions.

entries.covers: 2027/28 Code of Practice on Local Authority Accounting

release_schedule.rule: CIPFA LASAAC's development timetable targets publication of each year's Code of Practice on Local Authority Accounting no later than 1 April, ahead of the financial year it covers (e.g. the 2026/27 Code was 'aiming to have 2026/27 Code published in April 2026', and FRAB papers state 'the 2027/28 Code to be published no later than 1 April 2027'), following a summer/autumn consultation and exposure draft cycle.
release_schedule.note: The 2026/27 edition (this corpus's current annual edition) was targeted for publication by April 2026 per a CIPFA update to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government's UPAG panel (UPAG 13/01), and has presumably already been published by the current date (2026-08-11), since the 2026/27 financial year is already underway. The next edition, the 2027/28 Code, is committed by FRAB papers (FRAB 158, item 04A) to be published no later than 1 April 2027, following a consultation anticipated over summer 2026. No public release-calendar page with exact day-level dates was found; the CIPFA policy/guidance landing page itself returned a 403 error on direct fetch.

reports.title: Statement of Accounts 2024-25 (City of Wolverhampton Council)
reports.description: Chosen as the exemplar English local authority, the way Nijmegen is the exemplar Dutch municipality and Grande Prairie the exemplar Alberta one — its own accounting-policy notes and auditor's opinion both name the CIPFA/LASAAC Code by dated edition. VERIFIED DIRECTLY: 311-page PDF downloaded and text-extracted in full (pypdf); the Code is named 15+ times through the document.

release_schedule.rule: The Accounts and Audit (Amendment) Regulations 2024 (SI 2024/907), which inserted Regulation 9A into the Accounts and Audit Regulations 2015, require a Category 1 authority to publish its accountability statements (statement of accounts, together with the auditor's opinion/certificate, annual governance statement, and narrative statement) on or before a staggered statutory deadline for each financial year during the backlog-recovery period: 2023/24 by 28 February 2025; 2024/25 by 27 February 2026; 2025/26 by 31 January 2027; 2026/27 by 30 November 2027; 2027/28 by 30 November 2028.
release_schedule.note: This report (Statement of Accounts 2024-25) was already published by Wolverhampton in January 2026 (per the corpus url), ahead of its own statutory deadline of 27 February 2026 under SI 2024/907. The 'next' entry above is therefore the following year's edition, Statement of Accounts 2025-26, whose statutory deadline is 31 January 2027. Deadlines during this backlog-recovery period (through 2027/28) are staggered and non-uniform year to year by design, rather than a fixed annual date; from 2028/29 onward a different, presumably more regular, framework under Regulation 10 applies. releases_per_year=1 remains an accurate simplification (one Statement of Accounts is published per financial year).

reports.title: Local Non-Domestic Rating List / Council Tax Valuation List
reports.description: The national property-valuation function underlying both Council Tax bands and Business Rates rateable values — the UK functional equivalent of the Netherlands' `nl-wet-woz` and Ontario's `mpac-assessment`. Legal basis, VERIFIED DIRECTLY (legislation.gov.uk): Local Government Finance Act 1992 ss.20-23 (Council Tax valuation lists) and Local Government Finance Act 1988 ss.41, 61 and Sch.6 (business-rates rating lists and the 'rateable value' definition). NOTE ON NAMING: neither Act uses the literal string 'Valuation Office Agency' in the sections checked — both instead say 'the Commissioners of Inland Revenue' / 'the valuation officer' / 'listing officer'. 'Valuation Office Agency' as a literal name only appears in downstream documents (see `uk-stevenage-nndr1`) — flagged per this project's own tense/naming-precision convention rather than silently modernised.
reports.cadence_note: Business-rates rating lists are compiled on a multi-year revaluation cycle (1988 Act s.41(2): 1 April 1990 and every fifth year after, subject to later amendment); Council Tax valuation lists are maintained continuously. Filed as annual as the nearest practical cadence.

entries.covers: Next compiled Local Non-Domestic Rating List (England and Wales), 2029 revaluation

release_schedule.rule: Non-Domestic Rating Act 2023: from Royal Assent, business rates (non-domestic rating list) revaluations occur every 3 years rather than every 5, beginning with the list compiled 1 April 2026. New rating lists are compiled and come into force on 1 April in the revaluation year.
release_schedule.note: This corpus entry appears to bundle two distinct VOA products. (1) The Local Non-Domestic Rating List (business rates) now revalues every 3 years per the Non-Domestic Rating Act 2023 (2023 -> 2026 -> next 2029); the 2026 list was already compiled/in force by 1 April 2026, before today's date (2026-08-11), so the next compiled list is due 1 April 2029. (2) The Council Tax Valuation List (domestic property bands) has no fixed statutory revaluation cycle in England (irregular, last fully revalued 1991/2003 in Wales); Wales is separately pursuing a council tax revaluation reform (targeting new valuation lists around 2028) via the Local Government Finance (Wales) Bill, but as of this research no confirmed in-force date was found for that Welsh council tax revaluation - it remains a policy proposal under legislative development, not a scheduled release. If these are meant to be split into two separate corpus entries, the non-domestic rating list has the clearer stated-rule schedule (above); the council tax valuation list would be closer to 'irregular' (England) or a not-yet-finalized reform timeline (Wales).

_dropped.edge: UK Shared Prosperity Fund (UKSPF) succeeds EU structural funds (ERDF/ESF)
_dropped.why: UPDATED 2026-08-06. The original objection — 'does not fit this corpus's relationship_type ontology (calculated_from | uses_data_from | methodology_depends_on | cites — none of which mean replaces or succeeds)' — has been resolved at the schema level: `supersedes` is now a `RelationType` and this corpus has a parallel unweighted `relations` list to hold it. See `notes/SCHEMA-DECISION-relationship-types.md` and `src/lib/types.ts`. THIS CASE STILL CANNOT BE MINTED, for a reason the original note did not identify: NEITHER END IS A NODE. There is no `gb-ukspf-prospectus` and no node for the EU structural funds, so a relation would dangle at both ends and the loader would drop it. It is therefore reclassified from `note` to `no-node-yet` — a research lead with a known shape, not an ontology problem. The evidence is unchanged and the conflict in it is unchanged: the UKSPF prospectus's ministerial foreword states "This is our vision and ambition for the new £2.6 billion UK Shared Prosperity Fund (UKSPF), which succeeds the old EU structural funds" (VERIFIED DIRECTLY, gov.uk fetched and parsed), while the UKSPF's own FAQ page states, also VERIFIED DIRECTLY, "The UKSPF is not a direct replacement for EU structural funds." Two primary UK-government documents holding different framings of the same relationship, reported per `Research.1.md` §3 and not adjudicated — and note that this conflict is now a second-order problem: it decides what the relation's `basis` should say, not whether the relation can exist. Neither document names ERDF or ESF anywhere in the text fetched; a targeted search for those acronyms in both returned NOT FOUND. A subagent (not independently re-verified) reported an Orkney Islands Council committee report naming both "European Regional Development Fund (ERDF)" and "European Social Fund (ESF)" as the programmes UKSPF and the Levelling Up Fund replace. WHAT UNBLOCKS THIS: two nodes. The UKSPF prospectus is recurrently published and is the easy one. [RESOLVED 2026-08-07: both nodes now exist (gb-ukspf-prospectus, eu-esif-common-provisions-regulation) and the corpus's first `supersedes` relation is minted in src/data/research/gb-ukspf-succession.json, with the Orkney and North East Lincolnshire council citations verified first-hand and folded into its basis. This entry retained as the lead's history.]
